name: Email verification
needs: make sure users own the email they signed up with
people sign up with fake emails
someone signed up with my email address
let users change their email safely
summary: Sending a one-time link or code to the address a user gives and marking it verified only when they use it. It proves they own the inbox before you send them anything important or let that address reset a password.
need_when: Email is used for password reset, billing, invites or anything private.
Users can change their email address.
skip_when: Sign-in is only by magic link or a provider that already verified the email.

ways.title: Your auth library's verification
ways.how: django-allauth, Devise confirmable, Laravel MustVerifyEmail, Better Auth and Auth.js email flows.
ways.tradeoff: Handled for you. Decide whether unverified users can use the app at all.

ways.title: Hosted auth
ways.how: Clerk, Supabase Auth, Firebase Auth and Auth0 send verification emails and expose a verified flag.
ways.tradeoff: No code. Their email templates and sending domain unless you configure yours.

ways.title: Your own signed tokens
ways.how: A random token stored as a hash with user id, email and expiry, or a signed token with your framework's signer.
ways.tradeoff: Simple. Remember to bind it to the exact email being verified.

prompt:
Add email verification at signup and on email change.

Requirements:
- After signup, send a link with a random single-use token (stored as a hash) that expires in [24 hours]. The token is tied to the user id and the exact email.
- Until verified, allow [limited use] and block [billing, invites, exports].
- Resend button with a rate limit. Old links stop working when a new one is sent.
- Email change: keep the old address active, send the link to the new one, switch only after it's clicked, and notify the old address.
- Password reset never goes to an unverified address.
- The same "check your inbox" message whether or not the address exists, so the form can't be used to find accounts.
- Clicking the link while logged out still verifies, then asks the user to log in.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. A link works once and fails after expiry.
2. Changing email doesn't switch until the new address confirms, and the old address gets a notice.
3. A token made for one email can't verify a different email on the same account.
4. Resend is throttled.
5. Unverified accounts can't reach the blocked features through the API.
acceptance_checks: A link works once and fails after expiry.
Changing email doesn't switch until the new address confirms, and the old address gets a notice.
A token made for one email can't verify a different email on the same account.
Unverified accounts can't reach the blocked features through the API.
if_you_skip_it: Someone signs up with another person's email and later takes over their account, or your sending reputation sinks from typo addresses.
